## Purpose
`prompt_submit_inject.rs` and `session_start_inject.rs` are the two consolidated lifecycle-event modules: each rides a single Claude Code hook event (`UserPromptSubmit`, `SessionStart`) and folds several ordered concerns into ONE `Verdict::Inject`, because the dispatcher's fold is last-writer-wins — separate `Inject`s would silently drop all but one.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/hooks/session/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 2
Both exemplars open with a numbered/bulleted list in the module header naming every concern riding the event and the EXACT order they compose in (documented explicitly because order is load-bearing — e.g. "injectables first, banner next, writing rule last"). Each module exposes a unit struct (`PromptSubmitInject`, `SessionStartInject`) implementing `Check`, never `Observer`, because the composed advisory/banner is the return value. Concerns that are pure side effects (harness-init, spec-hygiene) stay `Observer`-shaped internally and are invoked from within the `Check::evaluate`, not exposed as separate top-level hooks.

## How to apply
A new lifecycle concern for `SessionStart` or `UserPromptSubmit` is added as a new ordered bullet in the relevant module's header and a new internal step in its `Check::evaluate`, composed into the single `Verdict::Inject` at the position documented — never as a new sibling `Check`/`Observer` on the same trigger, which would create the last-writer-wins collision these modules exist to avoid.
